payload.title: Section concept lists and their cards in every context pack
payload.description:
Ryan 2026-11-03: an editor configures, per section, the concepts that section should be especially aware of, and those concepts reach every agent's context pack. His example: the confinement problem and the containment problem in Security. Decisions: pre-baked cards first; an on-demand lookup for agents is a later ticket; automatic suggestions (PPY-b69b15) are a lower tier and a person's list always outranks them.

## Part 1: storage, command line, packs (one PR, merge to develop)

**Field.** `NewsroomSection.trackedConcepts: a.json()` in `amplify/data/resource.ts` and `schema.ts` (`npm run test:schema-parity`). A list of `{conceptLineageId, note, addedBy, addedAt}`. Editors can already update this model, so no new function or grant. Older sites do not have the field yet: follow how `NEWER_REFERENCE_FIELDS` in `graphql_authoring.py` reads a site whose schema lacks a field, so a router serving mixed versions keeps working. Check `editorial_context.find_section` and `safe_list_records("NewsroomSection")`.

**Command.** `papyrus sections concepts --section S` lists. `papyrus sections concepts add --section S --concept NAME [--note TEXT] [--create]` resolves a name, alias, `#hashtag` or node key to a current non-rejected node; an unknown name fails unless `--create`, which makes an `editor_concept` node with exactly the id and shape `ensureEditorConcept` in `amplify/functions/category-action/reference-links.ts` makes (write a Python equivalent and a shared fixture test so the two cannot drift). `remove` takes the same forms. `--dry-run`. Writes by default like the other commands.

**Pack.** `src/papyrus_content/newsroom_context_pack.py` (read its docstring; layers and profiles are data). Add to `SECTION_BLOCK`, first:
- `section_concepts`, core: one card per tracked concept: name, aliases, kind, description, the editor's note, and its links to other concepts by predicate, with the note a person wrote on the link. Person-accepted links first. Read relations with `list_semantic_relations_by_subject_state` and `..._object_state`; see `edge_notes` and `signal_inputs.explanation_of`. A tracked concept that no longer resolves or was rejected is a warning, not a card.
- `concept_references`, a ring: accepted References tagged with (`related_to`) or mentioning (`mentions`) a tracked concept, best first by `reference_rank`, one line each with `reference_one_line`, labelled with the concept. No fixed count; the budget bounds it. The Story's own References are left out.
Empty reason when the section tracks none. All three profiles get it through the block. Update the expected layer orders in `features_backend/newsroom-context-pack.feature`.

**Specs and docs.** Gherkin in `features_backend/section-concepts.feature` plus additions to the pack feature. `docs/newsroom-context-packs.md` updated. A p.apyr.us docs task is a separate later ticket; mention it in your report.

## Part 2: the UI (a second PR, LEFT OPEN for screenshot review; do not merge)

In the section's settings at `/newsroom/administration/sections`: a "Concepts this section tracks" area with the same typed `#` box as the Related section on a Reference (`components/related-section.tsx`, `components/reference-links-context.tsx`), including its "Create #name" action, and a row per concept with name, optional note and a remove control. On the concept page (`components/wiki-concepts-view.tsx`): "Tracked by" listing the sections, each with a way to add or remove. Rules: Lucide icons only, buttons and textareas, no dropdowns, flat background colours and rounded rectangles with no outlines or hairlines, never colour alone as a signal, the word "section" in copy and never "desk". Preview with `npm run dev:preview` (no AWS) and save screenshots at desktop and phone width under `/private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-home-Projects/01ea45fd-85a1-432a-89a4-a99b8de4198e/scratchpad/section-concepts/`.
